facts.text: Private cars can only drive as far as Täsch, and the last 7 km must be travelled by train or taxi.
facts.quote: Private cars can only drive as far as Täsch.

facts.text: A shuttle train departs from the Matterhorn Terminal Täsch every 20 minutes during the day, and there are 2,100 covered parking spaces.
Half-hourly trains run from Visp, which has connections to major Swiss cities and the Geneva and Zurich airports.
Zermatt has almost no internal combustion vehicles except occasional delivery and specialist services.
Buses run every 20-30 minutes depending on the time of day and year.
In general, anything in the village is at most a twenty minute walk away if you are fit.
facts.quote: at most a twenty minute walk away if you are fit

facts.text: During the high season, nearly 20,000 people are living in a town with only 5 or 6 streets, so expect crowds.
Local bus trips cost Fr. 2.50 on the green line and Fr. 3.20 on the red line, but are free with a ski pass or train ticket.
facts.quote: Fr. 2.50 on the green line and Fr. 3.20 on the red line

facts.text: A weekly pass with unlimited rides costs Fr. 22.
facts.quote: A weekly pass with unlimited rides costs Fr. 22.

facts.text: Zermatt is busier and much more expensive than other destinations in the region.
facts.quote: much more expensive than other destinations

facts.text: You can cycle or stroll in complete safety.
facts.quote: You can cycle or stroll in complete safety.

facts.text: Almost all vehicles in Zermatt are battery driven and almost completely silent.
